newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen up amid sideways drift.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen up amid sideways drift.

text.p: Polish shares eased in higher turnover and analysts said they could edge up on Thursday amid longer-term sideways drift, as the proximity of psychological support at 16,000 should spur some bargain-hunters.
The main market's WIG index fell 0.1 percent, to 16,222.4, and turnover rose 15.9 percent to 191.1 million zlotys ($61.6 million) on all three markets as 59 issues fell, 22 rose and 17 were flat.

"Buying was strong after price fixing, so there should be growth tomorrow, but the market is likely to stabilise later, as big investors prefer to wait for the (September) elections," said Artur Czerwonski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage.
Most banks, underperforming the market in the last three months, rose or were flat on Wednesday, but not much upside was seen, as they were unlikely to show good earnings in 1997.

Analysts said the market was likely to maintain its eight-week sideways drift as forthcoming large privatisations were likely to draw capital from the bourse and September elections were limiting buying.
But they said the Polish economy had excellent growth prospects and therefore significant falls were unlikely.
Banks rebounded or held flat on Wednesday after they fell an average 30 percent in the last three months.
Analysts said banks looked cheap at current prices, but they saw little potential for a significant earnings rebound this year after weak first quarter and therefore expected them to stabilise.
Bank Rozwoju Eksportu (BRE) was the main market's top gainer, jumping 9.9 percent, after it fell 40 percent since its February 13 52-week high.
Thirteen stocks rose, two fell and four were flat in 25- million-zloty (8.1 million) continuous trade.
